doc.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Vegas as security; the lounge jobs disappear
summary: Vegas jobs were secure until self-contained groups and piped music cut the lounges; Moody left wanting to play jazz.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: So there were a lot of jazz musicians there even though you weren't working playing jazz, still, a lot of you were there?

Well, what it was, see, at that time, Vegas was like a -- what do you call it? Security. Because you -- you had a gig and what happened was, when the union, like, folded with this little stuff and they started bringing in little self-contained groups -- .
Now, what -- what -- what was that?
Well, you know, I really don't know what it was, but they started bringing in self- contained groups and they started cutting music out of the lounges and things and piping in music.

There are no jobs in Vegas. You know, I got out of there just in time. I split, man, I wanted to because I got a divorce. And I wanted to play -- I wanted to play some jazz, man. Because, see when I was there, I didn't wanna play jazz. Because, first of all, there was no time for it. There was only time for that clarinet. You know, inside of, you know. Be able to get through those parts, you know? So, but I'd do it again if I had to, you know.
